2010_004_042010regmtg.paragraph: Board packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of Tuesday, April 20, 2010, at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan. It carries the agenda, winter all-state and senior scholar athlete recognitions, the minutes of March 16, 2010, and the March 2010 Treasurer's Report with fund-by-fund budget reports and the full Pentamation check register, followed by personnel, curriculum, business and policy items. Total disbursements in the period were $7,548,403.08. Item 6.D presents reductions in certified staff effective at the end of the day on June 30, 2010, attributed to the projected financial condition of the District and proposed 2010/2011 budget reductions.

**Meeting**
Troy School District Board of Education, Regular Meeting, Tuesday, April 20, 2010, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098 (district address 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000). Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 58 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW).

**Recognitions**
All-State winter athletes: George Abro (wrestling, Athens), Sara Lin (gymnastics, Troy High), Brooke Madzia (gymnastics, Athens; repeat Division 2 All-Around state champion, broke the state record for floor exercises), Miles McDonald (swimming, Troy High), Jacqlynn Stewart (gymnastics, Athens) and Jeremy Stoian (wrestling, Athens). **Identification.** Board packet for the Troy School District Board of Education Regular Meeting of Tuesday, April 20, 2010, 7:00 PM, at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098; district masthead 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000. Packet pages run to 129. Superintendent: Barbara A. Fowler, Ph.D.

**Recognitions.** All-State winter athletes: George Abro (senior, Athens, wrestling 145 lb), Sara Lin (sophomore, Troy High, gymnastics), Brooke Madzia (senior, Athens, gymnastics, repeat state champion in the Division 2 All-Around, state champion on vault, broke the state record for floor exercises), Miles McDonald (sophomore, Troy High, swimming), Jacqlynn Stewart (junior, Athens, gymnastics) and Jeremy Stoian (senior, Athens, wrestling 130 lb). Certificates were awarded to 47 senior scholar athletes from winter and spring sports, the criterion being a 3.5 cumulative grade point average while participating in an athletic program.

**Minutes of March 16, 2010.** Called to order by President Underwood at 7:04 p.m., with members Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart and Pochodylo, Superintendent Fowler, and approximately 175 additional members of the audience. Teacher of the Year honors went to Robin Couzens (Bemis) and Brian Nutting (Troy High) for 2008/2009 and to Lisa Carruthers (Leonard), Kristine Casko (Smith) and Pauline Walker (Athens) for 2009/2010. Resolution 10-025 added an anti-virus license renewal item, Yes 7, No 0. Andrea Moon spoke on the proposed budget reduction to the 5th grade vocal music program and Bruce Bloomingdale on agenda format. Recess 7:27 p.m., reconvened 7:32 p.m. Resolution 10-026 approved the March 2 and March 9, 2010 minutes, the January and February 2010 Treasurer's Reports and the anti-virus bid, 7-0. Resolution 10-027 adopted Literature, published by McDougal Littell, for English grades six through 12, phased in over two years: high school beginning 2010-2011 in the estimated amount of $469,369 and middle school beginning 2011-2012 in the estimated amount of $321,052. Resolution 10-028 awarded Athens media center furniture of $83,660.93 (Office Express $16,957.18, 3rd Coast $66,703.75); Resolution 10-029 awarded media center carpet to Conventional Carpet for $27,040.00; Resolution 10-030 awarded bus security cameras to Unity School Bus Parts for $49,895.00, all from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund and all 7-0. Resolution 10-031 moved to closed session under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c) to discuss TESPA negotiations, carried 7-0; closed session 9:01 p.m., reconvened 9:47 p.m., adjourned 9:48 p.m. Submitted by Nancy L. Philippart, Secretary.

**Item 5.C, library automation software.** Scott Bryan, Director of Technology, requested software bid through Oakland Schools bid #9.0041; the resolution awards Follett Software Company $62,601.00 from the 2010-2011 General Fund, recommended by Frank E. Lams, Supervisor, Purchasing and Budget, 1140 Rankin, Troy, MI 48083. Bryan's revised April 1, 2010 memo describes converting from self-hosted SirsiDynix Horizon to Follett Destiny hosted by Oakland Schools, fully live by September 30, 2010; the $62,601 conversion less the budgeted $12,074 leaves an additional 2010-11 request of $50,527. The SirsiDynix contract was renewed February 1, 2010 for $12,073.54 through January 31, 2011; Follett annual maintenance is $13,402.03, not due until after July of 2011. The cost analysis lists server upgrades of $2,500, 2011 server replacement of $12,000, media tech salary and benefits of $43,181, potential first year savings of $5,825, first year cost with tech staffed of ($48,027), and annual savings after staffing adjustment of $41,853. Media Technician Jill Valko has a total budget impact of $54,309 including benefits; Bryan writes that not filling her position would be a hardship and that he does not support making that cut.

**Personnel.** 6.A accepts retirements effective at the end of the school day on June 21, 2010: Kathleen Danielson (Niles Community High School, hired October 8, 1996), Jane Drotos (Hamilton, June 27, 1995), Ruth Frushour (Athens, November 10, 1975), Michael Heist (Boulan Park, July 3, 1978), Janis Hodgkins (Larson, November 19, 1976), Jane Juett (Leonard, December 9, 1985), Monica Lamb (Hamilton, February 26, 1980), Jean Brazelton-McGehee (Hamilton, September 3, 1991), Rosalie Mallory (Troy Union, July 12, 1973), Rosemary Morrow (Troy High, October 1, 1982), Leon Raczkowski (Costello, June 30, 1976), Linda Ruks (Boulan Park, September 19, 1976) and Alan Walthall (Boulan Park, September 6, 1977). 6.B accepts the resignation of Michael M. Adamczyk, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, effective June 30, 2010; a March 26, 2010 letter from Jasen M. Witt, J.D., Assistant Superintendent Human Resources, and Barbara A. Fowler acknowledges his March 24, 2010 letter, thanks him for the past 17 years, and notes his move to Chicago as Assistant Superintendent for Business and Auxiliary Services for Community Consolidated School District 15; he was hired in March 1993. 6.C grants tenure under the Michigan Teachers' Tenure Act to Josh Heppner (Athens), Kathryn Amaradio-Taylor (Baker), Andrea Lothian (Larson), Christine Russell (Morse), Kelly Paterson and Shannon Tonkin (International Academy - East). 6.D lists 66 certified staff reductions for 2010-2011 with layoff notice effective at the end of the day on June 30, 2010, consistent with the Tenure Act and the agreement with the Troy Education Association, citing the projected financial condition of the School District and the proposed budget reductions for the 2010/2011 fiscal year.

**Curriculum and business.** 7.A adopts the Teen Health textbook and supporting materials, including the human sexuality information, published by Glencoe and presented March 16, 2010, for the middle school health program, as an expenditure of the 2010-2011 secondary textbook budgets in the estimated amount of $17,193. 8.A awards 30 document cameras at $995 each, bid through the statewide REMC bid, for $29,850.00 from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund; the resolution names City Automation while the memoranda name City Animation. The cameras are a component of the Smart Board project, and of the 100 Smart Boards in this project, 30 will be going to secondary schools.

**Item 9.A, policy second reading.** Approves changes to B-1208, B-1211, B-1301, C-1402, K-1303, K-1304 and new D-1106, first read March 16, 2010. B-1208 Voting (adopted January 16, 1979) requires compliance with the Revised School Code and the Open Meetings Act, with roll call by random call of last names on a rotating basis. B-1211 Public Participation (revised April 1988, March 17, 1998, July 10, 2007, March 17, 2009) replaces the prior one-half hour period and five-minute turns with 60 minutes per meeting, generally 30 minutes at the beginning limited to agenda items and 30 minutes at the end limited to non-agenda items, a Speaker Request Form available 30 minutes before the meeting, and a three-minute limit per speaker with no transfer of time. B-1301 Agenda Format (revised September 28, 1988, October 3, 1989, March 17, 1998, June 19, 2007) lists items A through K, adding a second Public Communication before Other. C-1402 Smoking (adopted February 2, 1999, revised September, 2003) follows Public Act 140 of 1993 with the exception that smoking is prohibited at athletic fields. New D-1106 Fixed Asset Policy tracks items whose cost exceeds $5,000 with useful life exceeding one year, allows theft-prone items costing less than $5,000, and classifies assets as Land, Buildings, Improvements other than buildings, Construction in Progress and Machinery and Equipment. K-1303 (adopted May 3, 1976, revised January 16, 1979 and April 21, 1998) requires complete neutrality by school personnel including contracted personnel. K-1304 (adopted April 19, 1976, revised January 16, 1979, April 21, 1998, April 15, 2003) becomes Advertising on School District Property and in School District Electronic Media, declares that property a nonpublic forum, lists 16 prohibited product and use categories, and allows petition to the superintendent within 30 calendar days and a final decision within 30 calendar days.
